svg.title: Replaying one AgvMove, call by call
svg.desc: UML sequence diagram, animated: ScheduleEventDag::ApplyEventsTo walks the topological order; each event's virtual ApplyTo picks the subclass, std::visit picks the variant alternative, and overload resolution picks the DiscreteGarageState::OnEvent that checks and changes the state.
svg.metadata: ["A caller needs \"the garage after everything planned so far\": it copies ctx->initial_state into working_state and asks the event DAG to replay itself onto that copy.", "ScheduleEventDag::ApplyEventsTo computes a topological order and visits every event in it. Order matters: an AgvMove only succeeds if earlier events left the AGV where this one expects it.", "For one vertex the DAG holds a std::shared_ptr<ScheduleEvent>. Calling the pure-virtual ApplyTo runs AgvMove::ApplyTo through the vtable: the first choice, made at run time from the object's class.", "AgvMove stores discrete_change_, a std::variant<AgvLiftChanged, AgvPoseChanged>. std::visit reads which alternative it holds (index 1 here) and calls the lambda with that alternative: the second choice.", "The lambda body is one call, state.OnEvent(arg). The compiler already picked the overload for each copy of the lambda: OnEvent(const AgvPoseChanged&) here, OnEvent(const AgvLiftChanged&) in the other. This third choice costs nothing at run time.", "OnEvent checks the event against the state before changing it: the AGV exists, it is at node_id_curr@heading_curr, the move is not in place, and no other AGV is on node_id_next. It checks no geometry or edges.", "All checks pass: the AGV's pose becomes node_id_next@heading_next and OnEvent returns SucceededEvent(), {true, \"\"}. The BoolStringPair travels back unchanged through the lambda, visit and ApplyTo.", "The first failure stops the replay: ApplyEventsTo returns stdx::Unexpected(\"Event <event>: <reason>\") and working_state keeps every change made before it. Callers must treat that copy as spoiled."]

g.text: Each layer answers one question. The event DAG supplies the order, the event supplies the change, and DiscreteGarageState owns the rule. Messages stay on screen; the highlighted band is the current step.
